variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: missense, NP_000220.1:p.(Gly368Val). The papers describe the disease as autosomal recessive and caused by loss of LCAT function; the review also notes an intermediate (co-dominant) biochemical phenotype in heterozygous carriers.

quotes.quote: LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disease [4, 5].
Loss of LCAT function causes decreased maturation of HDL particles and increased HDL levels of unesterified cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine.

carriers of one mutant LCAT allele show an intermediate biochemical phenotype between homozygous carriers and controls, suggesting that the disease, which is reported as recessive, is indeed co-dominant for the biochemical phenotype.

concerns: The variant appears only in a systematic review table (34256778) without a case description; the review does not name the original publication in the row, so the person-level data are second-hand.
Zygosity, phase and family data are not given in the review; the batch row records zygosity as not reported.
Every clinical field for this person is 'Unk'.
Possible source is a population study of low HDL-C (reference [98] title), not a case report; the row does not name its source.
notes_for_panel: One supplementary-table row (author Cohen, USA) with all clinical fields unknown; the variant string also appears in the American row of Table 1 (cohort-level). The review's reference list contains Cohen JC et al. 2004, 'Multiple rare alleles contribute to low plasma levels of HDL cholesterol' (Science), a low-HDL population study, which may be the source; if so the carrier may have been ascertained for low HDL-C rather than LCAT deficiency. This link is not stated in the row.
